messages:
Maria: FYI bootstrapping apac-north-1 nodegroup failed during driver install. Kubelet crashloop on new p4d-24g hosts. @oncall can we triage?
Devin: Quick look — driver installer is pulling CUDA 12 packages but AMI appears baked with CUDA 11. Kubelet OOM/crash on nvidia module load.
Devin: log snippet:
```
[kubelet] E0412 08:10:05.123 kubelet.go:190] Failed to start containerd: exit status 1: modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia': Exec format error
Kernel messages: nvidia: version magic '5.15.0-101' vs '5.15.0-99'
```
Raj: Also seeing bootstrap failures fetching apt repos — subnet for nodegroup doesn't have a route to NAT gateway so the instances can't reach apt mirrors. That explains the partial installs.
ops-bot: Deployment event 2026-04-12T08:12:34 - rollback initiated for nodegroup apac-ng-1 (reason: kubelet crashloop & bootstrap timeouts).
Hao: We attempted an immediate rollback; cluster recovered but that left partial state on 4/20 nodes. Suggestion: pin driver version in the node-driver DaemonSet and prefer baking AMI with exact driver/kernel match before scaling.
Sarah: Short-term workaround: I SSH'd one host and used our internal apt mirror via HTTP proxy; that allowed the driver package + DKMS to finish and kubelet came up. But that's manual and doesn't scale.
Devin: I'm drafting a checklist for new-region runbook updates: AMI driver/kernel match, outbound route to NAT, SG egress rules, SSM + SSM-agent version, attached instance profiles, and a post-bake validation script (nvidia-smi, apt fetch, kubelet start).
Maria: Also a cost/quotas note: autoscaler requested lots of spot p4d capacity, some requests hit regional quota denial and the fallback attempted on-demand which tripped our budget alert. Need to tune spot fallback policy.
Raj: Can we cap spot usage at 40% of the nodepool during early bring-up? That would avoid mass quota failures while we validate.
Hao: Agreed. The capacity allocator should respect a "bring-up conservative" flag. I'll add that to the allocator config; low-risk canary pool = on-demand, rest = capped spot.
ops-bot: Pager alert acknowledged by Maria :eyes:.
ci-cd-bot: build/deploy job #8932 failed: apt-get timeout while installing nvidia-driver (see logs).
Devin: Action items (short):
1) Bake new AMI with CUDA12-compatible drivers and kernel modules matched to EC2 kernel.
2) Add route to NAT in the nodegroup subnets and validate outbound connectivity in preflight.
3) Limit spot usage for canary and early rollouts.
4) Add runtime validation (nvidia-smi, apt fetch, kubelet health) to the runbook and CI.
5) Hand off to relops for controlled rollout and quota checks.
Sarah: I'll open PR infra/ami-images with bake + validation tests (script will run apt fetch + sudo nvidia-smi + modprobe). ETA PR in 30m.
Maria: @Raj please coordinate with CS/sales about potential customer impact (none reported yet) — flag if any latency/errors surface.
Raj: Will ping CS and add a short status note. ETA for customer note: 45m.
Hao: Timeline: bake + run validations -> deploy to canary 2 nodes in ~2 hours, monitor 2 hours, if green start 50% rollout ~6 hours from now.
Maria: Sounds good — mark this thread resolved once canary passes validation. Thanks all :tada:
Devin: I'll update the runbook and add the new preflight checks.
Sarah: PR opened: infra/ami-images#278 — includes validation scripts.
Raj: CS notified, no customer reports.
Maria: Closing loop: will follow up in handoff doc and schedule a short postmortem if rollout problems persist. Thanks team.
